notes.text: Kranz says he created the term "tough and competent" after the Apollo 1 fire killed a crew on the launch pad.
notes.quote: when we had the Apollo 1 fire, I created the term tough and competent because I was absolutely killed by the fact that we had lost a crew in the launch pad

notes.text: Kranz says Chris Kraft trusted him to act as his deputy.
notes.quote: And Chris Kraft trusted me to act as his deputy.

notes.text: You can never lose it. If you do something, you have to walk the talk.
notes.quote: You can never lose it. If you do something, you have to walk the talk.

notes.text: Kranz says his first boss in flight test, Harry Carroll, taught him that communications are the key to success in every venture.
notes.quote: my first boss, Harry Carroll, in the flight test taught me that basically communications are the key to success in every venture that you're going to undertake.

notes.text: I said, I will stand behind every call you will make. We came into this room as a team and we will leave as a team.
notes.quote: I said, I will stand behind every call you will make. We came into this room as a team and we will leave as a team.

notes.text: They knew that whatever happened in that room, and boy, we had some bad times that day.
notes.quote: They knew that whatever happened in that room, and boy, we had some bad times that day.

notes.text: Kranz says the Gemini 8 emergency, with Neil Armstrong and Dave Scott aboard, forced a landing in the Pacific Ocean.
notes.quote: And we had two ships that had to be with Neil Armstrong and Dave Scott that basically we didn't want to take the chance of getting them around to proper landing sites. So we had to come down on the Pacific Ocean.

notes.text: So it's really something that is a key to accomplishing an objective that is high risk, because risk is the price of progress.
notes.quote: So it's really something that is a key to accomplishing an objective that is high risk, because risk is the price of progress.

notes.text: I like it because everything is black and white. There are no shades of gray. We either go or no go.
notes.quote: I like it because everything is black and white. There are no shades of gray. We either go or no go.

notes.text: Kranz says the "go" call came from fighter operations in Korea, where his crew chief saluted him before every taxi.
notes.quote: in aircraft operations, fighter operations in Korea, I had a crew chief. And every time I taxied out, he'd give me a hand salute, saying my aircraft was go.

notes.text: Kranz says he went through three generations of controllers and built a boot camp for the teams flying the shuttle.
notes.quote: I went through three generations of young controllers. And this is one of the things that we had to build into the teams flying the shuttle program. So we established a boot camp

notes.text: Focusing the accountability because we depend upon you. I depend upon you. The program depends upon you. We will fail without you.
notes.quote: Focusing the accountability because we depend upon you. I depend upon you. The program depends upon you. We will fail without you.

notes.text: Kranz says a special forces team in Afghanistan adopted "tough and competent".
notes.quote: I had a special forces team that adopted that over in Afghanistan.

notes.text: That's the price for admission to Mission Control.
notes.quote: That's the price for admission to Mission Control.

notes.text: Kranz says the line "failure is not an option" was created by Hollywood, not by him.
notes.quote: Well, there are two major themes. First of all, failure is not an option was created by Hollywood.

notes.text: Kranz traces the film to his controller Jerry Bostick, whose son worked with Imagine Entertainment and found that Jim Lovell was writing a book.
notes.quote: I had one of my controllers, Jerry Bostick, whose son, he went out to Hollywood. And basically, he started working with Imagine Entertainment. He found that Jim Lovell was writing a book,

notes.text: Kranz says what he actually said was that they had never lost an American in space and were not going to lose one now.
notes.quote: my real statement was, we have never lost an American in a space. We sure as hell aren't going to lose one now. This crew is coming home.
